Catalytic Asymmetric Synthesis of Inherently Chiral Eight-Membered
O-Heterocycles through Cross-[4+ 4] Cycloaddition of Quinone
Methides
Da Xu, Guojie Zhou, Bangli Liu, Shiqi Jia, Yidong Liu,* and Hailong Yan*
Abstract: Inherently chiral eight-membered rings embedded in tetraphenylene derivatives and hetero-analogues exhibit
unique properties and allow diverse applications. A conceptually viable and straightforward approach to these
frameworks is [4+4] cycloaddition, which still remains elusive. Herein, we describe the stereoselective cross-[4+4]
cycloaddition of quinone methides (QMs), leading to the formation of oxa-analogues of tetraphenylene with exceptional
chemo-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivity. The structures of these novel rigid eight-membered O-heterocycles were
explored by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, and their stereochemical stability was elaborated through both density
functional theory (DFT) calculations and thermal racemization experiments. The developed methodology exhibited
broad substrate scope and the resulting cross-[4+4] cycloadducts could be readily transformed into valuable chiral
building blocks. Our findings expand the library of inherently chiral medium-sized rings and also contribute to the
advancement of asymmetric cross-[4+4] cycloadditions of quinone methides.
Introduction
Chirality is an intrinsic property of molecular systems. The
design of new chiral molecular architectures and stereo-
chemical control are significant for asymmetric synthesis.<sup>[1]</sup>
Tetraphenylene with a rigid central eight-membered ring is
formed by ortho-annulation of four benzenes.<sup>[2–5]</sup> The entire
molecule with suitable substituents can create inherent
chirality,<sup>[6–16]</sup> which is distinct from the prevailing stereogenic
elements such as central, axial, planar, and helical elements.
Due to their unique chiral properties, tetraphenylene
derivatives are used as functional molecules and have
attracted considerable attention.<sup>[17–19]</sup> However, only Shibata,
Yang, and Zhu reported sporadic asymmetric synthetic
approaches for the construction of chiral tetraphenylene
derivatives and their aza-analogues (Figure 1A).<sup>[20–24]</sup> Nota-
bly, the challenge escalates when oxa-analogues are used as
target molecules. The incorporation of oxygen into the
central eight-membered ring increases the conformational
flexibility, so the inherently chiral eight-membered O-
heterocycles are elusive. Hence, it is significant to enhance
its inversion barrier by the structural modification of oxa-
analogue and develop the corresponding asymmetric cata-
lytic method of enantioenriched oxa-analogues of tetraphe-
nylene.
The [4+4] cycloaddition is conceptually recognized as a
straightforward and atom-economical approach towards the
eight-membered rings,<sup>[25,26]</sup> and has been successfully used to
forge chiral cyclooctadiene products by Dieck, Cramer, and
Jørgensen.<sup>[27–29]</sup> Nevertheless, the asymmetric synthesis of
eight-membered O-heterocycles through thermal [4+4]
cycloaddition was seldom reported due to the lack of
synthetic strategies and suitable cycloaddends. ortho-
Quinone methides (o-QMs) are highly reactive oxygenated
four-atom synthons in synthetic chemistry, medicinal
chemistry, and material chemistry.<sup>[30–34]</sup> The strong tendency
of rearomatization makes them strong electrophiles and
electron-poor heterodienes and valuable catalytic asymmet-
ric reactions involving o-QMs or its analogues have been
realized in recent years (Figure 1B).<sup>[35–53]</sup> Through the judi-
cious choice of reagents, the asymmetric [4+3], [4+2], and
[4+1] cycloadditions of o-QMs were well established.<sup>[54–67]</sup>
The [4+4] cycloadditions of o-QMs are still underdeveloped,
especially the cross-[4+4] cycloaddition of o-QMs (Fig-
ure 1B).<sup>[68,69]</sup> Except the control of the rapid reactivity of o-
QMs, the above challenge may also arise from the unfavor-
able entropic and transannular interactions in the generation
of medium-sized rings.<sup>[70–87]</sup>
Our group has been devoted to the development of
asymmetric reactions by manipulating vinylidene ortho-
quinone methides (VQMs), an o-QM analogue with an
allene motif. With suitable substituent patterns, VQMs
could retain the chiral feature and act as axially chiral
intermediates in asymmetric reactions.<sup>[88–107]</sup> We aim to
synthesize inherently chiral oxa-analogues of tetraphenylene
through a conceptually straightforward and atom-econom-
ical cross-[4+4] cycloaddition of VQM and typical o-QM.

Methides

broad substrate scope and the resulting cross-[4+4] cycloadducts could be readily transformed into valuable chiral
building blocks. Our findings expand the library of inherently chiral medium-sized rings and also contribute to the
advancement of asymmetric cross-[4+4] cycloadditions of quinone methides.

Yang, and Zhu reported sporadic asymmetric synthetic

bly, the challenge escalates when oxa-analogues are used as
target molecules. The incorporation of oxygen into the
central eight-membered ring increases the conformational
flexibility, so the inherently chiral eight-membered O-
heterocycles are elusive. Hence, it is significant to enhance

analogue and develop the corresponding asymmetric cata-

nylene.

straightforward and atom-economical approach towards the

able entropic and transannular interactions in the generation
of medium-sized rings.<sup>[70–87]</sup>

asymmetric reactions by manipulating vinylidene ortho-

allene motif. With suitable substituent patterns, VQMs

synthesize inherently chiral oxa-analogues of tetraphenylene

However, due to the highly reactive nature of these polyene
species, o-QMs and VQMs could generate various products
due to complicated chemoselectivity (Figure 1C), such as [4
+4]-isomers derived from competitive cross- and homo-
cycloaddition and other polymerization products. Moreover,
the thermal stepwise [4+4] cycloaddition could result in a
large number of possible stereoisomers (Figure 1C). Except
for selectivity, the stereochemical stability of the target
saddle-shaped eight-membered O-heterocycles needs to be
further verified.
Results and Discussion
Based on the above consideration, the preliminary computa-
tion was performed with o-QM 2a and VQM I as model
substrates to elucidate the possible chemically distinct
products (Figure 2). The relatively stable and separable o-
QM 2a could efficiently compress the self-polymerization.
VQM I could be generated in situ from the precursor 2-
alkynylnaphthol 1 a in the presence of a Brønsted base
catalyst and bromine source. The computation results of the
cross-[4+4] cycloaddition of o-QM 2a and VQM I revealed
a stepwise process and the predicted barrier for the
transition state TS 1 was 24.9 kcal/mol. The transition state
TS2 and TS3 for the homo-[4+4] cycloaddition of VQM I
or o-QM 2 a respectively resulted in significantly higher
energy barriers, indicating that the cross-[4+4] cycloaddition
of o-QM 2a and VQM I yielded good chemoselectivity.
Moreover, the calculation results of the pathways related to
diastereoisomers indicated higher energy barriers (TS 4–6)
than TS1, thus leading to the predicted good diastereose-
lectivity.

generation and cross-[4+4] cycloaddition were separately
performed. Thus, the enantioselectivity of VQM I formation

substrates to elucidate the possible chemically distinct

Based on the initial calculation results, we examined the
reaction between VQM I and o-QM 2a. The methodology
was a two-step one-pot protocol, in which the VQM I
generation and cross-[4+4] cycloaddition were separately
performed. Thus, the enantioselectivity of VQM I formation
could be improved by tuning reaction conditions and the
stereocontrol of the subsequent cross-[4+4] cycloaddition
relied on the chirality conversion. Delightedly, the reaction
between VQM precursor 1 a and NBS in toluene at �78 °C
in the presence of quinine A delivered axially chiral VQM I
intermediate and subsequent reaction quenching and addi-
tion of o-QM 2a at room temperature afforded the cross-[4
+4] cycloadduct 3a in 50% yield and 76 % ee with excellent
diastereoselectivity (> 20 :1). The observed chemo- and

improve the enantioselectivity of the whole process, a range
of quinine derivatives B–K were examined (Table 1 and
Supporting Information). Ultimately, catalyst I provided the
highest selectivity for the construction of 3 a. A survey of
different solvents revealed that toluene still had superior
enantioselectivity (see Supporting Information). Increasing
the reaction temperature in the first step did not improve
the yield significantly, but the enantioselectivity was signifi-

similar ee value (Table 1, entry 8), whereas 1,8-diazabicyclo
[5.4.0] undec-7-ene (DBU) totally suppress the reaction

The crystallographic analysis revealed that compound 3 o
possessed a bridged axially chiral styrene with an eight-
membered linkage. The entire molecule featured a saddle-
shaped geometry and the central eight-membered O-hetero-
cycle was a boat conformation (Figure 3A). The stereo-
chemical stability of 3a was then probed by thermal
racemization experiments and the enantiomeric and diaster-
eomeric ratios in toluene respectively at 60 °C and 90 °C for
8 h showed no significant change (see Supporting Informa-
tion). To further investigate the stability of eight-membered
O-heterocycles conformers, we calculated the inversion
barriers for compounds 3 a and their analogs (3–I with
central chirality removed, 3–III with olefin axial chirality
removed, and 3–V with both central and axial chirality
removed). The computational results indicate that the
synthesized oxa-eight-membered ring exhibits significant
rigidity, with an interconversion energy barrier of 48.2 kcal/
mol. This rigidity is primarily attributed to the bulky
alkenes. while the stereogenic carbon center of compoun-
d 3a has only a marginal influence on the interconversion
barrier (Figures 3C–E).
To elucidate the synthetic potential of these cyclo-
adducts, we performed various transformations of com-
pounds 3a and 5a (Figure 4). The treatment of 3a with
aluminum trichloride led to the cleavage of one ether group
with acetone as nucleophile and afforded the axially chiral
ether 3 aa without obvious reduction of enantioselectivity.

alkenes. while the stereogenic carbon center of compoun-
d 3a has only a marginal influence on the interconversion
barrier (Figures 3C–E).
To elucidate the synthetic potential of these cyclo-
adducts, we performed various transformations of com-
pounds 3a and 5a (Figure 4). The treatment of 3a with
aluminum trichloride led to the cleavage of one ether group
with acetone as nucleophile and afforded the axially chiral
ether 3 aa without obvious reduction of enantioselectivity.

The cyanation of 3a was conducted with CuCN in DMF at
1 0 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }
to produce 3ab in moderate yield with similar
enantioselectivity. The sequential hydrogenation of 3ab
gave access to the axially chiral ether 3ac. Moreover,
product 5a could be selectively oxidized to furnish the
corresponding p-quinone methide 5aa in excellent yields
with similar enantioselectivity. The simple treatment of 5 a
with p-toluenesulfonic acid delivered spirocyclic 5 ab. It was
assumed to be realized through an acid-promoted remote
elimination and subsequent addition to the in situ generated
p-quinone methide by the naphthol moiety in an enolate C-
alkylation fashion. When a stronger Lewis acid such as
BF ·OEt was used, compound 5a was reverted back to the
starting VQM intermediate. This intermediate was then
trapped by H O, leading to the formation of 5ac–1 after
undergoing keto-enol tautomerism. Subsequently, the chiral
dihydronaphthofuran 5 ac, featuring vicinal tertiary carbon
stereocenters, was obtained through a reaction with lithium
aluminum hydride. The structures of 3aa, 5 ab, and 5ac were
unambiguously determined by single-crystal X-ray diffrac-
tion analysis.<sup>[108]</sup>
Conclusions
In conclusion, we illustrated a novel asymmetric synthetic
approach of inherently chiral eight-membered O-hetero-
cycles through cross-[4+4] cycloaddition of quinone me-
thides with vinylidene ortho-quinone methides. The devel-
oped reactions proceeded in high efficiency with excellent
selectivity. As a novel oxa-analogue of tetraphenylene, the
desired eight-membered O-heterocycles also featured the
saddle-shaped orientation and exhibited high geometric
rigidity. The theoretical investigation revealed that the
hindered rotation of the embedded axially chiral styrene
helped to fix the conformation of the target eight-membered
O-heterocycles. This study offered a general synthesis
approach to the inherently chiral medium-sized ring system
and expanded the application scope of QMs for higher-order
cycloaddition reactions.
